questions.q: Tell me about the content you have written. What types (blogs, social posts, product pages), for whom, and how often?
questions.looks_for: Real examples, audience and brand, type of content, regular volume, and their own role from research to final draft.

questions.q: Describe a piece you wrote that got good results or feedback. What made it work?
questions.looks_for: Specific piece, the result (views, leads, client praise), and why: clear audience, research, strong headline, simple structure.

questions.q: How do you change your writing when the reader is a busy shop owner instead of a college student?
questions.looks_for: Adjusts tone, words, length and examples to the reader; short and practical for the shop owner; shows audience thinking.

questions.q: What does writing for SEO mean, and how do you add keywords without making the article sound unnatural?
questions.looks_for: Writing content that matches what people search; keyword in title, headings and naturally in text; answers the reader's question first.

questions.q: Why is copying content from other websites a problem, even if you change some words?
questions.looks_for: Plagiarism, unfair to the writer, search penalties, brand trust; original research and own voice are expected.

questions.q: A client sends back your article saying it is boring and wants it rewritten by tomorrow, but gives no other details. What would you do?
questions.looks_for: Asks a few quick questions or checks their brand samples, revises hook, examples and structure, delivers on time, stays positive about feedback.

questions.q: Why do you want this content writer job, when can you join (state your notice period), and what salary do you expect?
questions.looks_for: Clear reason linked to the work, states notice period or joining date in days or weeks, and gives an expected monthly or yearly salary figure or range without dodging.
